about: Owner-declared entries of the v4 resolve / traverse deploy gate (gate_policy.py --declared): what the MCP surface cannot show, and the v4 suite errors that block every v4 gate on a quiet host too (to be removed when the v5 manifest fixes them), decided by the owner, never inferred from an answer a run received. Each entry names its evidence. Pending the owner's review before the policy is pinned.

exclusions.reason: the MCP's traverse_capabilities answers the service's view (gate, backends, service_maxima, presets), not the host's document (table case capabilities.traverse_capabilities_document: 'the raw document and its gate-block projection are not exposed'), so its one property check, capabilities_doc, is not exposed ('field not in the answer: release') and every MCP execution is inconclusive; nothing else is tested there. Tested on direct-local.

v4 suite error (triage-v4 V02, manifest v5): labels.max_seed_labels 10,000 makes the 6,181 derived headers exhaust the scenario's 512 MB modelled memory budget at 58 of 200 bp on every direct execution (memory is modelled, not load-dependent), so walk_in_record is inconclusive; excluded on MCP already (advanced path).

v4 suite error (triage-v4 G18, manifest v5): max_work_units 300,000 is below the seed phase's cost (at least 435,722 units on 6f945db4), so the seed fails before any walk on every arm and repeat and nothing is tested.

by the scenario's design (triage-v4 V04, EXPECTED): repeat 1 resends repeat 0's run-unique attempt_id, the host answers the planned 409 duplicate, and the 200-only checks (invariants, answer_fields) are not testable on it; repeat 0's attempt test stays required.

not_required.reason: the MCP's traverse records carry no label dictionary ('field not in the answer: results[0].label_dict' on every MCP execution of v3 and v4, VERIFY-B); the walk itself (walk_in_record) stays required on the MCP arm, label_dict_contains on direct-local.

the service merges identical seeds before sending (table case traverse.duplicate_seeds), so the duplicate's result (results.1.duplicate) cannot exist in the MCP answer; the merge itself is the by-design pair direct-local verifies, answer_fields stays required on direct-local.
